records.question: What was the overall mean fish biomass at NPSA from 2010–2019 (in g m-2)?
records.ground_truth_answer: Overall mean fish biomass was 72.7 ± 122.4 SD g m-2 from 2010–2019.
ground_truth_chunks: Fish biomass estimates ranged from 3.5 to 1,879.8 grams (g) m-2. Overall mean was 72.7 ± 122.4 SD g m-2 from 2010–2019.
Fish biomass was generally lower in Vatia Bay, which was skewed by the high biomass value from a single large, round ribbontail stingray (*Taeniurops meyeni*) in the western section of the park.

records.question: How many transects were sampled each year and how were they divided between fixed and temporary transects?
records.ground_truth_answer: Thirty transects were sampled each year, split into 15 fixed (permanent) transects that were re-sampled annually and 15 temporary transects that were randomly selected each year and sampled only once.
ground_truth_chunks: A split panel design was used with 30 belt transects (25 m long x variable width) sampled annually between 2007 and 2019.

Fifteen fixed (permanent) transects were randomly selected at the onset of the monitoring program in 2007 and marked with galvanized steel pins for relocation purposes. These sites were subsequently re-sampled each year.
The remaining 15 temporary transects were randomly selected each year of monitoring and sampled only once.

records.section_heading: Trophic Composition of the Fish Assemblage
records.question: What percentage of the total numerical density of fish at the National Park of American Samoa from 2010–2019 were planktivores?
ground_truth_chunks: Planktivores comprised 45% of the total numerical density with 29% as other secondary consumers.

records.question: Which predictor appeared to be the strongest for all fish assemblage metrics?
records.ground_truth_answer: The presence of crustose coralline algae (CCA) appeared to be the strongest predictor for all fish assemblage metrics.
ground_truth_chunks: The presence of CCA appeared to be the strongest predictor for all of the fish assemblage metrics due to the larger F statistics, with higher cover of CCA associated with higher values for most fish assemblage characteristics.

records.question: Which R command in the section generates the table of Count, Mean, SD, and SE of Richness by Year and Loc_Type?
records.ground_truth_answer: meanse<-summaryBy(Richness~Year*Loc_Type, data=Fish, FUN=function(x) c(count=length(x), mean=mean(x), sd=sd(x), se=sd(x)/sqrt(length(x)))) followed by print(meanse).

records.question: What does the logit function defined in the section return, and how is it applied to the Fish data?
records.ground_truth_answer: The logit function is defined to return sqrt(x). It is applied with Fish$LogitDensity<- logit((Fish$Density)), creating LogitDensity as the square-root of Density.
ground_truth_chunks: logit<-function(x) return(sqrt(x)) # Transform the data if it is right skewed. Better than log for NPSA 2010-2019 data.
Fish\$LogitDensity<- logit((Fish\$Density)) # Creates a variable called LogitDensity, which is the square-root of the density.
